name: Sphinx
body:
The sphinx is a contradiction as difficult to reconcile as their esoteric riddles. While classically known for guarding lairs in an eternal vigil, the feline sphinx is an apex predator capable of flying for miles in pursuit of prey. While often a symbol of reclusive intellectuals and wise philosophers, the sphinx’s boundless arrogance and merciless anger rivals even the fiercest dragons.

Sphinxes are determined and proud magical beasts that value their convictions and self-image. While a sphinx may spend decades in solitude working out a satisfying answer to life’s greatest questions, they have a natural desire to test their mental and physical acuity, pairing both ideas and claws against worthy adversaries in an endless pursuit of self-perfection. They are fascinated with the thought processes of other species, using complex traps and multi-faceted riddles as a way to learn how others approach solving a problem. They will patiently watch their subjects struggle with their puzzles for hours like a cat playing with its food, only to mercilessly rip them to pieces once they are satisfied. This dichotomy of patience and self-worth makes the sphinx a valuable guardian to deities and other great powers willing to offer the sphinx a suitable lair, knowing the proud beast would never stymie their reputation by breaking a pact.

If you want to play a proud magical beast who loves to solve problems, improve themselves, and values power, you should play a sphinx.

You Might…
Think very highly of yourself.
Have an obsession with answering one or more great questions.
Enjoy overcoming competitive challenges, especially riddles, games, and puzzles.
Others Probably…
Think you are a dangerous and unpredictable monster.
Assume you are a font of endless knowledge who can see the future.
Believe they can control you with riddles.
Physical Description

Sphinxes are large beings with the body of a lion and the wings of a bird. Most sphinxes have the torso and head of a human, often accentuated with long ears and a row of glistening razor-sharp teeth. Other sphinxes have the heads of animals and include the hawk-headed hieracosphinx, the ram-headed criosphinx, and the jackal-headed sakalisphinx.

Most sphinxes reach adulthood at 50 years of age, but beast-headed sphinxes like hieracosphinx tend to mature much more quickly. A sphinx can live for hundreds of years, but their exact lifespan is hard to pin down given their solitary lifestyle and penchant for magic. There is a myth that a sphinx who lives for 2,000 years becomes a being of pure knowledge, their essence absorbed into the Akashic records, but most sphinxes are reluctant to discuss this legend with outsiders, and may not even know the truth of it themselves.

Challenging Anatomy

Playing a monstrous PC such as a sphinx presents many unique challenges that should be discussed with your GM during character creation. Many of these concerns can be offset by playing a sakalisphinx or using the Two Feet at Noon ancestry feat to transform into a Medium-sized humanoid. In its base form, a sphinx adventurer can still cast spells and equip magic items. The only manufactured weapon a sphinx can wield in its base form is the clawblade. Despite being Large and normally taking up a 10-foot-by-10- foot space, a sphinx is a quadruped that can occupy a 5-foot-by-10-foot space without squeezing. A sphinx still requires and must occupy a 10-foot- by-10-foot space when using its wings.

Society

Most sphinxes are more driven by an urge to solve problems than foster a community. Some become so frustrated when they can’t figure something out that they retreat into a lair for centuries, while others develop an insatiable wanderlust to journey for answers. Most sphinxes will only stay together for short periods to exchange ideas or mate, hunting and protecting their young in nests or communal lairs until their cubs grow to maturity and are driven by the same urge to seek out their own wisdom.

Some scholars distinguish male and female sphinxes as androsphinxes and gynosphinxes. Some sphinxes accept these outmoded labels when it satisfies their ego, but there is no significant distinction between a male and female sphinx in terms of physical power or magical potential. Sphinxes will sometimes broker deals with other powerful creatures and deities, often entering a pact to protect a powerful artifact in exchange for a magnificent lair. Sphinxes have been known to spend time with dragons exchanging lore or even sharing an especially sprawling domicile, especially dragons that enjoy riddles.

While all sphinxes each have individual nuanced inclinations, there are strong cultural traditions among many of the sphinx ancestries which can be passed down parent-to-child for generations.

Many of these include a disdain for any other types of sphinxes. Each view the others as either challenges or mockeries of their greatness. Other traditions include treasure-hoarding for a criosphinx, who often buy extravagant lairs or secrets to impress other powerful entities. Aggressive hieracosphinx traditions place a much higher value on pure strength and encourage the defeat an enemy by force rather than using magic and riddles. The hawk-headed sphinxes sometimes band with other hieracosphinxes to take out a particularly powerful rival, but these alliances rarely outlive their targets. The traditions of the sakalisphinx are the most sociable, and assume they’ll mate for life, often living in pairs or packs. Many of the jackal-headed sphinxes are driven to interpret the underpinnings of other civilizations and will disguise themselves to experience the cultures firsthand.

Alignment and Religion

Their practice of ontology can push sphinxes toward neutrality. Many revel in succeeding under strict guidelines, seeing any set of rules as the parameters of a challenge to be met, granting them an affinity for law. The pragmatic traditions of hieracosphinx prioritizes results, which cause some of them to turn to evil as they allow the ends to justify any means. Community-minded sakalisphinx are the sphinxes with a society that is most inclined toward good. Chaotic sphinxes are often shunned by their kin, believed to have been driven from the path of order by a maddening paradox.

Sphinxes are rarely devout, paying only as much reverence to gods of knowledge and truth as they would other powerful sphinxes. The most common relationship between a sphinx and a deity are pacts of mutual respect, often for a lair protected by a god of duty, magic, protection, and time. There is a cult of sphinxes who seek out the Akashic records and believe they are the true inheritors of the esoteric plane.

Traits
Ability Score Modifiers: Sphinxes are quick learners, but their patience makes them slow to react. They gain +2 Wisdom, and -2 Dexterity.
Magical Beast: Sphinxes are magical beasts.
Normal Speed: Sphinxes have a base speed of 30 feet.
Flight: Sphinxes have a spy speed of 30 feet with average maneuverability. Until a sphinx is 5th level, they must end their movement on the ground at the end of each turn or fall.
Large: Sphinxes are Large and take a –1 size penalty to their AC, take a –4 size penalty on Stealth checks, and gain a +1 size bonus on combat maneuver checks and to combat maneuver defense. A sphinx can take up just a 5-foot-10-foot space without squeezing when not using their wings.
Darkvision: Sphinxes can see in the dark up to 60 feet.
Akashic Scholar: Sphinxes are natural scholars who absorb certain types of information more easily than most races. They choose three Knowledge skills and always treat those skills as class skills. If they take a class that grants any of those Knowledge skills as class skills, they gain a +1 racial bonus on the overlapping skill or skills.
Bellowing Roar: As a standard action you can let loose a terrifying roar. Attempt Intimidate checks to demoralize each enemy within a 20- foot cone. A creature you fail to demoralize is immune to your bellowing roar for 24 hours. This is a sonic mind-affecting fear effect. Once you use your roar, you can’t use it again unless you rest for 10 minutes.
Natural Weapons: Sphinxes have a pair of claws they can use as natural weapons. These claws are primary attacks that deal 1d6 points of damage.
Languages: Sphinxes begin play speaking Common and Sphinx. A sphinx with high Intelligence score can choose from the following: Akashic, Draconic, Necril, Terran, and up to one Ancient language.
Subraces
Criosphinx

The ram-headed criosphinxes are known for their relentless pursuit of wealth as a means of confirming their superiority, often buying needlessly large lairs filled with exotic menageries. They have a gore attack that deals 1d6 points of damage. They always treat Appraise and Intimidate as class skills. If they take a class that grants either or both of those skills as class skills, they gain a +1 racial bonus on the overlapping skill or skills. A criosphinx use speak with animals as a spell-like ability at will.

This replaces Akashic Scholar and Bellowing Roar.

Hieracosphinx

The falcon-headed hieracosphinxes are known for their pragmatic determination, focus on physical might, and sharp beaks. They have a bite attack that deals 1d6 points of damage. They always treat Perception and Fly as class skills. If they take a class that grants either or both of those skills as class skills, they gain a +1 racial bonus on the overlapping skill or skills.

This replaces Akashic Scholar.

Sakalisphinx

The jackal-headed sakalisphinx are known for their passion for ethnology, ability to disguise themselves as another race, and their powerful jaws. They have a bite attack that deals 1d8 points of damage. They always treat Diplomacy, Disguise, and Knowledge (local) as class skills. If they take a class that grants either or both of those skills as class skills, they gain a +1 racial bonus on the overlapping skill or skills. They can assume the appearance of a specific single medium-sized humanoid form. They require two days of downtime to perfect their form and always take that specific form until they spend the same amount of time adjusting their disguise. A sakalisphinx in humanoid form gains a +10 racial bonus on Disguise checks made to appear as a member of that species. Changing shape is a standard action. A sakalisphinx in humanoid form remains in humanoid form even if knocked unconscious or killed until it chooses to change form. A sakalisphinx of 5th level or higher can assume a hybrid form as a move action, gaining access to their natural weapons and wings. A sakalisphinx in hybrid form does not get any bonuses on Disguise checks.

This replaces Akashic Scholar and Bellowing Roar.

Alternate Racial Traits
Riddlemaster

Some sphinxes prefer to save their majestic voices for more cerebral challenges. You gain one riddle feat as a bonus feat. Add +1 to the Difficulty Class for all skill checks attempted to answer your riddles. This replaces Bellowing Roar.

Racial Feats

Sphinx culture is ancient and perceptive enough to know that sometimes, it’s better to blend in than to appear to be the greatest, fiercest creature present. While not all sphinxes have the natural ability to take a humanoid form, all can learn to master such abilities given time. The following feats represent the eventual mastery of such powers. 5

Two Feet At Noon

Prerequisite(s): Sphinx

You assume the appearance of a specific single medium-sized humanoid form. You gain a +10 racial bonus on Disguise checks made to appear as a member of that species. Changing shape is a standard action. You remain in humanoid form even if knocked unconscious or killed until you choose to change form. This otherwise functions as alter self, except it does not adjust your ability scores and you can stay in his form indefinitely.

Three Feet In The Evening

Prerequisite(s): Sphinx, Two Feet at Noon

You can assume a hybrid form when you transform using Two Feet at Noon. You may use your wings and your natural weapons while in hybrid form. You do not get a bonus to Disguise checks to appear as a member of that species.

Riddle Feats

Whether as a means to test a mortal or teach a valuable lesson, sphinxes have become almost synonymous with riddles. Over the centuries, the mystically inclined species has developed the means to weave magic into their words, posing questions whose very words carry extraordinary powers. Answering these riddles can overcome these effects, but giving a wrong answer can backfire. Each time you use a feat the riddle can change, but each feat’s riddle follows a specific theme. The mystical nature of these riddles causes them to manifest in a universal language any sentient creature can understand. The riddle itself always gives a clue as to the consequences of failing to successfully answer the riddle. Verbally answering a riddle requires a standard action and a successful skill check against DC 10 + 1/2 x the sphinx’s character level + the sphinx’s Wisdom modifier. If a riddle feat allows a saving throw to resist its effects, the DC is equal to 10 + half the sphinx’s level + the sphinx’s Wisdom modifier.

These feats can be taken by any sphinx or dragon. On rare occasions, other species can access these powers thanks to an open-minded mentor willing to teach these closely guarded secrets. These feats can be selected as a revelation or hex by any class with the corresponding class feature. If they do, calculate the Difficulty Class of the Riddle Feat as though it were a hex or revelation. The character must still meet all prerequisites of the riddle feat normally.

Riddle Me This…

Many sphinx abilities involve a challenging riddle. Some game groups may enjoy trying to solve an actual riddle, but others will prefer picking an appropriate associated skill. PCs looking to use riddles should discuss this with both their GM and the rest of the players at the table. It can be a rewarding experience and add a layer of verisimilitude to the game but don’t be afraid to mix and match the two concepts in a way that works for everyone in the group. The following ideas may help facilitate integrating riddles into your game:

Players or GMs attempting to answer a riddle could be given a specific amount of time for each attempt.

The Wayward Sphinx and Enigmatic Riddle abilities are very different, and some game groups may find themselves using riddles for one, but skill checks for the other.

Riddles should be prepared in advance. You can prepare a riddle for every monster in a dungeon, or save it for the most significant Knowledge check in an adventure.

Other players at the table could be allowed to solve a riddle, even if presented to an NPC. This can be especially helpful if there is a player at the table who loves riddles almost as much as a sphinx.

Riddle of Paradoxes

Prerequisite(s): character level 6

Benefit(s): You can utter an enigmatic riddle capable of confusing even the most learned sages. Choose one target who can hear you. The target must succeed at a Will save or get a circumstance penalty to their AC and on attack rolls, saving throws, skill checks equal to your Wisdom modifier until they attempt to answer your riddle as a free action. A creature who succeeds is immune to the riddle of paradoxes for 24 hours. Any other creature who heard the riddle can attempt to answer it for the target as a standard action, but suffers the incorrect answer effect if they fail to answer the riddle. Once you use this riddle, you can’t use it again unless you rest for 10 minutes.

Riddle: The riddle can be solved using Linguistics, Knowledge (planes, or religion) or Spellcraft.

Correct Answer: If a creature successfully answers your riddle reduce the DC required to answer your next riddle by 4 for 24 hours.

Incorrect Answer: A creature who incorrectly answers the riddle is confused for 1d4 rounds.

Riddle of Protection

Prerequisite(s): character level 9

Benefit(s): You can cast glyph of warding as a spell- like ability once per day. You or an ally may store a harmful spell or spell-like ability of 3rd level or lower into the glyph if you select a spell glyph. The glyph takes the physical form of a riddle written in magic script that any intelligent creature can read. The password to this glyph is always the correct answer. You can have two of these glyphs at a time, and using this ability again while two glyphs are active dismisses the oldest glyph. The glyph created by Riddle of Protection is a magic trap and can be disabled by characters with trapfinding.

Riddle: The Riddle of Protection is written on a door, wall, or across the floor and only requires a DC 10 perception check to see. The riddle can be solved using Knowledge (arcana, local, nature, planes, or religion), or Spellcraft.

Correct Answer: Any creature who successfully answers the riddle can safely bypass, deactivate for 1-minute, or automatically disable the trap.

Incorrect Answer: A creature who incorrectly answers the riddle activates the trap. If the spell used in the glyph has a saving throw, the spell uses the riddle’s saving throw instead of its own, if higher.

Riddle Of Stone

Prerequisite(s): character level 12

Benefit(s): You can create a non-magical stone statue in your likeness as creation 1/day. The statue remains indefinitely, but you can only have four statues in existence at a time. Casting this spell again when you already have four statues causes the oldest one to crumble into sand. You can concentrate for 1 minute to transfer your consciousness to any duplicate within 1 mile per character level. A statue created with this feat cannot be made into a living sphinx with the stone to flesh spell.

Riddle: The Riddle of Stone becomes etched onto the forehead of the statue until it becomes affected by Riddle of Life. The riddle can be solved using appraise, craft (stonework), Knowledge (planes), or sense motive.

Correct Answer: Any creature who successfully answers the riddle can force the consciousness of the Sphinx to become trapped in the statue for 1 hour, after which time the statue crumbles to dust.

Incorrect Answer: A creature who incorrectly answers the riddle of life must succeed at a Will save or its consciousness becomes forcefully transferred into the statue for 1 hour.

Riddle Of Patience

Prerequisite(s): character level 15

Benefit(s): You can turn into stone as a standard action, melding all your gear into your person and becoming an inert statue as flesh to stone. You can’t move, but can still take purely mental actions while in your petrified body. You are never mindless when turned into a statue and can always use this ability to reverse the petrification as a standard action, even if you are turned to stone by another effect.

Riddle: The Riddle of Patience becomes etched onto your chest so long as you are petrified. The riddle can be solved using appraise, craft (stonework), Heal, Knowledge (nature), or Use Magic Device.

Correct Answer: Any creature who successfully answers the riddle can force you to remain in statue form or return to flesh for up to 1 hour.

Incorrect Answer: A creature who incorrectly answers the riddle must succeed at a Fortitude save or be turned to stone, as flesh to stone, for 1 hour.

Riddle Of Life

Prerequisite(s): character level 18, Riddle of Patience, Riddle of Stone

Benefit(s): When you transfer your consciousness into a stone duplicate using Riddle of Stone, you can also transfer your absorbed gear into that statue. Once per week, you can use Riddle of Patience to become a flesh and blood sphinx using a duplicate you created with Riddle of Stone. The statue that was once your original body crumbles to sand.

Riddle: The Riddle of Life becomes etched onto your wings for 1 week after becoming a flesh and blood sphinx using a stone duplicate. The riddle can be solved using Heal, Linguistics, Knowledge (arcana), or Spellcraft.

Correct Answer: Any creature who successfully answers the riddle can forcefully petrify your body as the flesh to stone spell. You cannot use the Riddle of Patience to undo this petrification as long as the Riddle of Life remains, but you can still use the Riddle of Stone to transfer your consciousness to another body.

Incorrect Answer: A creature who incorrectly answers the riddle must succeed at a Fortitude save or be turned to stone, as flesh to stone, for 1 week
